definitions.explanation: A person who avoids work or effort. Can also refer to the animal sloth, which is named for its perceived laziness.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{怠|なま}け{者|もの}だ。
{怠|なま}け{者|もの}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれたくない→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧。
examples.english: I don't want to be called lazy.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{怠|なま}け{者|もの}だった⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{大人|おとな}→大人：02856_otona⟧になって⟦{変|か}わった→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧。
examples.english: I was lazy as a child, but I changed as an adult.

notes:
USAGE:
Formed from ⟦{怠|なま}ける→怠ける：02379_namakeru⟧ (to be lazy, to slack off) + ⟦{者|もの}→者：12734_mono⟧ (person). A fairly direct and somewhat harsh label. The word is also used as the Japanese name for the sloth (the animal), written as ナマケモノ in katakana.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {怠|なま}け{者|もの}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれる→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧ (to be called a slacker)
- {怠|なま}け{者|もの}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧レッテル (the label of being lazy)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ぐうたら→ぐうたら：27861_guutara⟧: lazybones — more casual and slightly humorous
- {横着|おうちゃく}: lazy, cutting corners — emphasizes taking shortcuts
